issues.t: Automatic transmission slips, shudders or fails
issues.sym: Shuddering at highway speed, slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, loss of second gear, or no movement at all.
issues.why: The GM-sourced 4-speed automatic in these Isuzu-built Passports wears out, and the torque converter clutch is a common source of shudder. Transmission failure is the top owner complaint for 1998 and 1999, and 1997 owners report check-transmission warnings.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it shudders or slips, get a diagnosis before it fails completely; a fluid change will not fix internal wear.

issues.t: Rear suspension bracket and frame can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the SUV wandering, or heavy rust and holes in the rear frame.
issues.why: Road salt rusts the frame where the rear lower suspension link mounts. The bracket can separate, which affects steering and handling. Honda recalled 1998-2002 Passports to inspect, treat or reinforce the bracket, and owners report frames rotting through at the rear.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the rear frame inspected. If the bracket or frame is rotted, do not drive until it is repaired.

issues.t: Passenger air bag may not inflate correctly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash. The passenger air bag might not inflate properly, or its module could rupture.
issues.why: Two recalls cover 2001 Passports: some passenger inflators had the wrong amount of propellant, and others were built without a check valve pin.
issues.next: Check your VIN and make sure the passenger air bag was replaced.

issues.t: ABS can lengthen stopping distance (recall)
issues.sym: The truck takes longer than expected to stop when the ABS activates, especially on rough or slippery roads.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake control logic could release brake pressure too much. A recall program installed a revised ABS control program.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the ABS update done if it was missed.

issues.t: Rear lower link nut can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the rear suspension, or the rear end feeling loose.
issues.why: Paint was applied unevenly where the rear lower link bolts on, so the nut could lose its tightness. Honda recalled these years to replace the nut and bolt.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the rear suspension bolts inspected.

issues.t: Engine wiring ground can break and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine will not start or stalls while driving.
issues.why: A ground terminal in the engine wiring harness was not crimped properly and could crack. Honda recalled these trucks to replace the harness.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN and make sure the repair was done.

issues.t: Fuel pump port can develop pinholes and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or wet spot near the top of the fuel tank.
issues.why: Fuel contaminated with silicon could eat pinholes in the fuel pump feed port. Honda recalled 2002 Passports in Texas and nearby states to add a cover or replace the pump.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and have it checked. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Paint and body rust problems
issues.sym: Peeling or flaking paint and rust bubbles on body panels.
issues.why: Body and paint complaints are the worst category for this Passport, with 2001 rated the worst model year.
issues.next: Wash off road salt often and treat rust spots early before they spread.

issues.t: Frame rusts through
issues.sym: Flaking rust and holes in the frame rails, clunks from the suspension, or a failed safety inspection.
issues.why: Frame rust is the top complaint for 1996 and 1997 Passports. Road salt and trapped moisture eat through the frame over time.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected on a lift before buying or before a long trip. A badly rotted frame is a safety risk and is often not worth repairing.

issues.t: Engine knocking or failure at high mileage
issues.sym: A knocking noise from the engine, low oil pressure, smoke, or the engine quitting.
issues.why: Owners of 1996 Passports report engine knocking and engine failures, usually past 130,000 miles. Worn bearings from age, low oil or overheating are the usual causes on engines this old.
issues.next: Check the oil level often. If the engine starts knocking, stop driving it hard and get a diagnosis; continuing to drive can destroy the engine.

issues.t: Drive belt squeals and wears out
issues.sym: A squeal from the engine at start-up or when turning the steering wheel, or a cracked, shiny belt.
issues.why: The accessory drive belt wears and glazes, and a weak tensioner or worn pulley makes it slip.
issues.next: Replace the belt and check the tensioner and pulleys. A broken belt stops the alternator and power steering.

issues.t: Poor FM radio reception
issues.sym: FM stations fade, crackle or drop out where other cars pick them up fine.
issues.why: Owners of the new 2026 Passport report weak FM reception. The cause has not been confirmed; antenna connections and amplifier faults are the usual suspects.
issues.next: Report it to a Honda dealer while the vehicle is under warranty so they can check the antenna and connections.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, will not start, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank can fail. Honda recalled these Passports to replace the fuel pump module.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN and have the pump replaced.

issues.t: Front frame welds may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning, but crash protection may be reduced.
issues.why: Some 2019 Passports were built with front frame side members not fully welded to the body. Honda inspects them and buys back or replaces affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN right away.

issues.t: Hood can fly open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The hood does not latch firmly, or pops up while driving.
issues.why: The hood latch striker can be damaged so the hood does not stay latched. Honda recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Do not drive if the hood will not latch.

issues.t: Continental tires may have a sidewall defect (recall)
issues.sym: A bulge in the tire sidewall, vibration, or a sudden loss of air.
issues.why: Some original Continental tires were overcured during manufacturing and could crack in the sidewall or separate.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the tires inspected. Replace any tire with a bulge right away.

issues.t: Backup camera image delayed or missing (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera image shows up late or not at all, and some gauges may go blank.
issues.why: Software faults in the network and gauge modules, and a faulty camera cable connector, can block the camera image. Honda recalled these vehicles for software updates and a new cable harness.
issues.next: Check your VIN for all three recalls. Look behind you until it is fixed.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor fault can affect the air bag (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger air bag status light shows the wrong setting, or the air bag warning light comes on.
issues.why: The weight sensor in the front passenger seat can crack and short, so the air bag may not turn off for a child or could deploy when it should not.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Keep children in the back seat until the sensor is replaced.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can separate from the booster (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, or less braking power than normal.
issues.why: A tie-rod fastener between the brake master cylinder and booster may have been assembled wrong at the factory.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN. If the pedal feels different, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Rear subframe can rust at the suspension mounts (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, odd tire wear, wandering, or visible rust and cracks near the rear suspension.
issues.why: In salt-belt states, the rear subframe can rust at the suspension mounts until it cracks. Honda recalled these vehicles to inspect and add a reinforcement kit.
issues.next: Check your VIN and book the inspection, especially if you live where roads are salted.

issues.t: Steering gearbox ball joint can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk when turning, loose-feeling steering, or pulling to one side.
issues.why: An inner ball joint housing in the steering gearbox may loosen and detach, which can cause loss of steering control.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have it inspected right away.

issues.t: Fuel filler neck tube can separate and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or fuel dripping near the rear wheel, especially after filling up.
issues.why: The fuel filler neck tube and pipe can separate and leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and get the recall done.

issues.t: Rear subframe bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the rear, or the rear end feeling unstable.
issues.why: Some rear subframe bolts were not tightened enough at the factory. Honda recalled these vehicles to inspect and replace the bolts.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get it inspected before long trips.

issues.t: Engine may not restart after Auto Idle Stop
issues.sym: At a stop, the engine shuts off as designed but then fails to restart, or stalls.
issues.why: Owners report restart failures with Auto Idle Stop. Weak batteries make it worse, and software updates have not fixed every vehicle. Honda issued bulletins 23-008 and 23-009, and NHTSA opened an engineering analysis (EA25004) that lists 2024 and 2025 Passports as well.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and ask a dealer about software updates. Turning off Auto Idle Stop with the button avoids the problem.

issues.t: 9-speed automatic makes harsh or jerky upshifts
issues.sym: Now and then the transmission bangs or jerks into the next gear while you speed up gently and steadily.
issues.why: Honda traced this to the transmission computer learning the wrong shift values. Its bulletins 19-124 and 20-029 cover every 2019 Passport and some 2020s.
issues.next: Ask a Honda dealer to check for the transmission software update. After the update the computer needs about 500 miles of normal driving to relearn, so give it time before judging the result.

issues.t: Engine won't crank after rain or snow and a hard freeze
issues.sym: On the first start of a freezing morning after wet weather, you press the start button and the engine does not crank at all. It may start normally once the weather warms up.
issues.why: Water can get inside the starter motor and freeze, locking it so it cannot turn the engine. Honda bulletin 23-023 covers 2019-2023 Passports.
issues.next: If it won't crank, check that the battery is strong. If it is, have a Honda dealer check the starter for this bulletin. A tow to a warm shop may get it going, but the starter and its relays usually need replacing.

issues.t: Accessory running board lights flicker or stay off
issues.sym: On Passports with Honda's lighted running boards, one or more of the step lights flickers or doesn't come on.
issues.why: Honda bulletin 20-022 says the running board light assemblies themselves are often faulty, after a blown inline fuse or a loose connector is ruled out.
issues.next: This is not a safety problem. Have the inline fuse and plug checked first; if they're fine, the lights are replaced as a set.

issues.t: Taillight or brake light stops working
issues.sym: A taillight or brake light stays out, and a fuse may be blown. Drivers behind you may not see you braking.
issues.why: Honda has asked dealers to send in 2022-2025 Passport Black Edition and TrailSport models with a taillight or brake light that keeps failing, so it can find the cause. No fix has been published yet.
issues.next: Walk around the car with someone pressing the brake. If a light is out, get it to a Honda dealer soon and mention Honda's taillight inspection request, since a dead brake light raises the risk of being rear-ended.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking activates with nothing ahead
issues.sym: The SUV suddenly brakes hard on its own, sometimes with a brake message on the dash, even though nothing is in the way. Owners say this has happened on highways and in rain.
issues.why: Several 2026 owners have filed complaints with NHTSA about unexpected braking from the collision mitigation system. No recall, bulletin or investigation has been issued yet, and the cause is not known.
issues.next: If it happens, note the time, speed and weather and report it to a Honda dealer and to NHTSA. Keep the windshield camera area and front radar clean. Ask the dealer to check the camera and radar aim and for software updates.
